verdict.rationale: Keycloak is itself a standards-based OAuth 2.0/OIDC authorization server. Its docs cover the building blocks an MCP auth flow needs: a well-known discovery endpoint, dynamic client registration, token introspection for validation, revocation, and client-credentials and device grants for agents. Nothing in the evidence ties this to MCP or confirms compliance with the MCP authorization profile, so the fit is plausible but unproven. Missing for 10: any MCP-specific documentation or guide, PKCE/OAuth 2.1 and resource-indicator/audience-bound token evidence, protected-resource-metadata support, explicit scope configuration evidence, and independent hands-on reports of fronting an MCP server.
